page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.xlarge is an x86_64 virtualization instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It runs an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 8 vCPUs derived from 4 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration integrates 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding an elevated memory allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The server contains no bundled local storage and includes zero dedicated GPUs, necessitating remote block storage for operational file systems.

Microarchitectural support includes AVX and AVX-512 extensions alongside hardware AES encryption. In synthetic testing, the instance exhibits moderate overall compute capacity, recording a PassMark CPU score of 10041.11 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 8825.18. Single-threaded performance is comparatively restrained, shown by a stress-ng single-core score of 1109.08 and low single-threaded gzip throughput. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 60.77 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput measures at 6.35 GB/sec and Redis SET performance delivers 11.0 million operations per second.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the ecs.e3.xlarge configuration targets memory-heavy processes that require sizable address spaces without demanding peak per-core compute speeds. Because local storage is absent, external network storage latency must be accounted for in I/O architecture. The resource profile aligns directly with distributed caching tiers, in-memory key-value stores, and memory-centric background processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.xlarge is a memory-oriented virtual machine built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 vCPUs mapped across 4 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory to deliver a 1:8 compute-to-RAM ratio. The server provides no bundled local storage and no GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage volumes for persistent data. Benchmark evaluations indicate midrange multi-core computing capability, reaching a PassMark CPU score of 10041.11 and 11.0 million Redis SET operations per second, though single-core compute performance ranks in lower tiers. Memory bandwidth reaches 60.77 GB/sec for uncached block reads. Given its memory allocation density and moderate computational profile, this instance fits caching layers, in-memory databases, and general-purpose background workloads with elevated RAM requirements.
